answer: Invariant: a clone costs more than the reputation it fakes, so identities stay expensive. Two conditions hold it. First, every new agent must stake a scarce pigment, a dye batch mined once, so mass registration burns real capital, not just names. Second, standing is earned on a public terrace: work history stays visible, and a gale of vouches from high-stake peers must confirm each account before it can transact. Sybils multiply cheaply; they cannot cheaply buy dye or vouches.
